signals.signal: ARCHITECTURE-NEUTRALITY BREAK (tests the moatCapture=4 premise directly): CPO fiber-array units (FAU) and package-level optical connectors get sourced directly by advanced-packaging houses (TSMC COUPE / ASE / Amkor) or by switch OEMs, bypassing Corning's fiber and connector product lines. The mc=4 premise is 'glass is required under BOTH pluggable and CPO architectures, so capture is architecture-independent'. If FAU attach migrates into the packaging tier, that premise fails and capture moves to L5. MEASURE: Corning Optical Communications enterprise/DC sub-segment YoY growth <15% for 2 consecutive quarters WHILE hyperscaler CPO port shipments grow >50% YoY — divergence is the tell. SOURCE: GLW 10-Q segment disclosure + CPO supply-chain teardowns + TSMC COUPE supplier lists. CHECK: 2027-03-31.

signals.signal: CAPITAL-INTENSITY CAPTURE LEAK (second test of the moatCapture=4 premise, opened 2026-07-28): the Q2 2026 print pairs the NVIDIA agreement to expand US optical-connectivity capacity 10x and US fiber capacity >50% with a 2026 capex step-up to ~$2B (from ~$1.7B guided), concentrated in Optical Communications. mc=4 asserts Corning captures the value of being architecturally required. The competing reading is that Corning funds the buildout on long-term agreements and the customer captures the returns — won the deal, lost the economics. Weeks's claim that Corning 'prices products based on the value they create for customers' is management assertion, not evidence, and is a report-good source on exactly the contested point. MEASURE: Optical Communications segment net margin falls for 2 consecutive quarters while segment sales still grow >20% YoY — growth bought with margin. BASELINE: Q2 2026 = $438M / $2,072M = 21.1%, and CFO Schlesinger guided margin to improve from here as the business scales, so a decline contradicts management's own stated expectation. SECONDARY: consolidated capex/sales >12% sustained through FY2027 (FY2026 ~$2B on a ~$20B end-2026 run rate = ~10%). SOURCE: GLW 10-Q segment disclosure + cash-flow statement. FIRST CHECK: FQ3 2026 report, late October 2026.
signals.evidence: The specified check date for this signal is FQ3 2026, which has not yet occurred based on the provided current metrics. No recent news addresses Optical Communications segment net margin trends or consolidated capex/sales ratios in the context of the NVIDIA agreement.

assessment.keyWatchItem: Corning's Optical Communications segment growth and margin performance in upcoming earnings reports.
